note: GENERIC TEMPLATE -- this file is the committed shape/schema a fork copies to create its own real runner-inventory.json (fork-local, holding real repo names/runner names/service accounts -- see this repo's README.md for the recommended fork-local-file convention). It contains exactly one clearly-fake, annotated example entry and no real infrastructure data. Tracks every Windows LabVIEW runner VM built on this host by vm/windows-labview/provision-windows-labview-vm.yml and Register-WindowsRunner.ps1, so vm_name/winrm_host_port/runner names never collide as more repos are onboarded. Add a new VM to the batch queue by appending an entry with "status": "queued" (including a real runnerName/runnerLabels/dedicatedServiceAccount -- register-runner needs them, see below) and running vm/windows-labview/batch-provision.sh, which updates this file automatically as it progresses (queued -> provisioning -> ready-for-activation or failed). Only the human-gated activation step (status -> active) and brand-new queued entries are edited by hand -- see the 'Batch-build runner VMs for multiple repos' runbook section in README.md. 'vncPort' (optional, schema@3+) pins the loopback VNC port vnc-console.sh uses for this VM's activation console; if omitted it's derived from winrmHostPort. 'guestHostname'/'guestFullName' (optional, schema@4+, issue #69) let you pin a real, human-chosen in-guest hostname/account-full-name per VM; if either is omitted, batch-provision.sh derives a unique fallback (a short hash-based hostname fitting Windows's 15-character NetBIOS limit, and a 'VM Builder (<vm_name>)' full name) instead of the old behavior of every VM in a batch silently sharing the exact same hostname.

statusValues.queued: Not yet started; batch-provision.sh will pick this up on its next run.
statusValues.provisioning: batch-provision.sh is actively running create-vm/install-vipm/install-labview/register-runner for this VM.
statusValues.ready-for-activation: VIPM + LabVIEW installed and the GitHub Actions runner is already registered and online; waiting on a human to activate LabVIEW/VIPM (interactive, cannot be automated -- the one remaining gate).
statusValues.failed: A phase failed; see the notes field for which phase and the workflow run conclusion. Safe to re-queue after investigating.
statusValues.active: Activated by the human operator after the 'Activate LabVIEW + VIPM' runbook step; runner was already registered automatically.

hostCapacity.notes: PLACEHOLDER -- fill in your own host's real CPU core count and total memory before provisioning, and periodically re-verify real available headroom with `free -h`/`df -h` rather than trusting a stale figure here. Each Windows guest in provisioning-manifest.json's default profile needs 8GB RAM/4 CPUs; running multiple concurrently can exhaust host RAM/disk well before this count's naive sum would suggest -- budget conservatively and prefer serial builds (batch-provision.sh's default behavior) over manually parallelizing them.

vms.notes: EXAMPLE ENTRY -- replace vmName/winrmHostPort/vncPort/targetRepo/runnerName/runnerLabels/dedicatedServiceAccount/guestHostname/guestFullName with your own real values before setting status to "queued" for real. Keep winrmHostPort/vncPort/guestHostname unique per VM on the same host to avoid port/hostname collisions. guestHostname/guestFullName are optional (schema@4+) -- omit either to get a derived, still-unique fallback instead.
